title: Build a set from its source
statement: For questions that share one source, choose the source first, list the distinct reasoning moves it supports, and write each question around a different move.
example: In one 100-item build, 12 of 19 shared-source sets failed, against 3 of the other 81 items.
detail: The pipeline's expectation matrix and pass contract both tell the writer to choose the source first, then work out distinct reasoning moves and write each question around a different one (`icloud-work/evaluatorML/.agent/memory/analysis/2026-05-25-ap-history-ib-expectation-matrix.md`, `icloud-work/evaluatorML/.agent/memory/analysis/2026-05-25-ib-pass-contract-matrix.md`). Shared-source sets failed far more often than other types: in one 100-item build, 12 of 19 sets failed, against 3 failures among the other 81 items (`icloud-work/evaluatorML/.agent/memory/e2e_pipeline/apush_unit1_deterministic_build2_eval/evaluation_report.md`). The later repair rules fixed one move per question: an outside cause or context, then a comparison or continuity, then a consequence (`icloud-work/evaluatorML/.agent/memory/e2e_pipeline/iterate_repair_to_100.py`, lines 202-204).
against: none found; no run isolates the effect of the build order.

evidence.quote: - Choose stimulus first, then create distinct child reasoning moves.
- build set backwards from stimulus: identify distinct APUSH reasoning moves first, then write each child around a different move.
Question 1 must ask for the outside historical cause or context that best explains the stimulus, not what the stimulus says.

The set must cover related but nonduplicative operations. A source can support identification, inference, context, value or limit, and causal connection, but four stems should not ask the same question with altered wording.
